analysis: Examined the three changed files in the batch. (1) ProviderLoop+Testing.swift head 141-151 adds two internal test seams, setVerifiedWeightHashesFileForTesting and setLoadWeightHasherForTesting. They are internal (not public) and are only reachable via @testable import. The file also has pre-existing seams that are not #if DEBUG-gated. These seams can redirect the verified-hash file and replace the weight hasher, which would matter to T-012/T-027 weight integrity if they were reachable in production. Nothing supplied shows a production caller. (2) ProviderLoop+Trust.swift line 129 adds GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice.report(failureMessage:modelID:) inside recordModelLoadError. Its implementation is not supplied, so I cannot tell whether it logs or prints, or writes files or runs subprocesses (for example sysctl for the wired limit). Inputs are the load-failure message and model ID, which are provider-local diagnostics. They contain no consumer prompt data (A-001) as far as the supplied code shows. The existing daemon-state path is unchanged. (3) ProviderLoop.swift adds loadWeightHasher, defaulting to WeightHasher.computeHash (same as the existing modelSwitchWeightHasher), and verifiedWeightHashesFile, which is nil until run() serves with host services. These are only declarations in this batch. The security-relevant behavior lives in the unsupplied captureWeightHash, finalizeReusableSSDLoad, VerifiedWeightHashStore and run() changes. The questions for the next pass are: whether VerifiedWeightHashStore writes at owner-only permissions with atomic, no-follow I/O; whether a recorded hash can be trusted at registration without being recomputed (T-012/T-027/T-034, SEC-007); whether cacheEligibleWeightHash binding to the SSD cache (T-041) is fail-closed; and whether GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice has side effects. No concrete regression is evidenced in the supplied lines, so there are no findings. Because these implementations were not supplied, I mark needs_deeper_review.
